If a line for the same work is `active` or has an open PR, do not redo it: continue that branch or pick other work. 2. **Claim it:** add one line at the top of the log with status `active`. 3. **Before you stop:** update your line with the status (`done`, `PR #n`, `blocked: reason`) and the next step. Commit and push it with your work. Never stop with unlogged work. 4. One line per piece of work, newest first. Details go in the PR, not the log. Line format: `YYYY-MM-DD | agent | branch → PR | status | what | next step` ## Brand rule Everything visual or written for TAKATAK follows `BRAND.md` (logo, colours, tagline, services). Electric blue on deep navy; never the old gold "TK" logo; green is for status only. ## Project continuity Keep `docs/PROJECT_STATUS.md`, `docs/TASK_QUEUE.md`, `docs/AGENT_HANDOFF.md`, `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` and `docs/DECISIONS.md` current. Log only verified CI, deployment and service statuses; do not publish secrets in this public repository.

items.title: TAKATAK Architecture Standard
items.summary: GROUPE TAKATAK is the central platform authority.
items.search_text: # TAKATAK Architecture Standard ## Central authority GROUPE TAKATAK is the central platform authority. The reusable platform pattern is: ``` TAKATAK Identity/Auth ↓ TAKATAK Dashboard / Control Plane ↓ shared services and APIs ↓ independent product applications ``` Child products keep their own domain UX and domain data. They should not create a second master identity system and should not directly couple to sibling applications. ## Shared central services Reusable TAKATAK platform capabilities include: - Identity / authentication / OTP - organizations, workspaces, brands and locations - roles, permissions and entitlements - billing and subscription services - notifications - SMS / voice / email - social account connections - reviews / reputation - content / blog / CMS - analytics - integrations and connector vault - webhooks - agent / automation services ## Data-access rules - Server-side authorization is authoritative. - Browser clients do not receive privileged database credentials. - Prisma/database access remains server-side. - Product authorization must not rely on editable user metadata. - Audit important writes. - Verify webhook signatures. - Use idempotency for externally-triggered state changes. - Never log secrets/tokens. ## Product isolation A product may reuse TAKATAK services without exposing unrelated product data. Recommended hierarchy: ``` Platform └─ Workspace └─ Client / Organization └─ Brand └─ Location └─ External accounts / domain records ``` ## Source-of-truth rule GitHub repositories are the engineering source of truth. Knowledge TakaTak stores the decisions, contracts and project memory needed to understand and evolve them.

items.title: Knowledge Ingestion Policy
items.summary: Capture reusable project intelligence without confusing original evidence with AI-generated interpretation.
items.search_text: # Knowledge Ingestion Policy ## Goal Capture reusable project intelligence without confusing original evidence with AI-generated interpretation. ## Knowledge record layers ### Source layer Stores provenance: - source system - source identifier - source repository/file/thread - timestamp when available - author/actor when appropriate - original excerpt or approved source artifact reference - content hash - ingestion timestamp ### Derived layer Stores: - summary - topics - project/domain - entities - decisions - implementation rules - dependencies - supersedes / conflicts-with relationships - retrieval tags Derived content must never be presented as a word-for-word source when it is not. ## Classification Allowed product domains: - product - website - design - engineering - integration - infrastructure - deployment - marketing-system - business-system - prompt - agent-instruction - project-history While this repository is public, private/sensitive categories are blocked from commit. ## Mixed conversations Do not ingest an entire mixed conversation just because part of it concerns a project. Segment source material first, then retain only the product-relevant portion for this repository. ## Conflict handling When two historical statements conflict: - keep both provenance records when useful, - mark the current decision, - record the date/reason for supersession, - never silently rewrite history. ## Future ingestion sources Potential approved sources: - ChatGPT exports/history - repository docs/issues/PRs/commits - Google Drive project documents - GitBook - project emails when explicitly approved and non-sensitive - exported Lovable project specifications - deployment runbooks - infrastructure documentation ## Security Credentials and secrets are never knowledge content. Store only the name/purpose of a secret and where it is managed securely.

items.title: Deployment Standards
items.summary: Primary infrastructure source snapshot:
items.search_text: # Deployment Standards ## Source precedence Primary infrastructure source snapshot: - `GROUPE TAKATAK — Plan maître Contabo VPS - Coolify - Migration A→Z.md` - reference date: **2026-09-30** ## Principle GitHub validates. Coolify deploys. A server must not become the place where broken builds are repaired manually. ## Central TAKATAK target The Contabo VPS becomes the central heavy application runtime for TAKATAK while other infrastructure can continue serving responsibilities that fit it. High-level flow: ``` Developer / Lovable ↓ GitHub ↓ CI ↓ approved branch ↓ Coolify ↓ Docker build ↓ health check ↓ release ``` ## Required CI gates Before production: - typecheck - lint - tests - production build - security checks - artifact checks when present - migration/rebuild validation when applicable **FAILED CI → NO PRODUCTION DEPLOYMENT** ## Branch/release direction Preferred flow: ``` feature branch ↓ PR ↓ CI ↓ staging ↓ QA ↓ main ↓ production ``` Never develop directly inside a production container. ## Runtime-isolation target The platform should not become one giant Node process. Target runtime responsibilities include: - `takatak-web` - `takatak-api` - `takatak-worker` - `takatak-social` - `takatak-webhooks` - Redis - `qmaps-api` - `flexs-api` These may initially originate from one monorepo. The important objective is runtime isolation, not repository proliferation. ## TAKATAK Web Responsibilities: - Dashboard/UI - SSR/public pages - auth presentation - account/billing UI - marketplace UI - social UI ## Central API direction A central TAKATAK API should own shared contracts such as: - customer/site API - integration API - master identity - QMAPS/FLEXS integration - orders - invoices - services - permissions - organizations Connected TAKATAK sites should speak to the central API rather than directly to each other. ## Workers Background workers handle: - analytics sync - social sync - email - notifications - report generation - site synchronization - CRM events - background imports - scheduled tasks - retry jobs A worker crash must not take down the Dashboard. ## Webhooks Webhook service requirements: - signature verification - idempotency - timestamp/replay validation - logging without secrets - retry handling - quick HTTP acknowledgement - heavy work pushed to a queue ## Redis Redis is for: - queues - locks - rate limiting - temporary caching - job coordination Redis should remain private to the service network unless a specific external need exists. ## Secret handling Do not commit secrets. Existing encryption/token keys that protect live data must be copied exactly during migration and never casually regenerated. Critical infrastructure decryption material must be backed up securely outside the server and never stored in GitHub, chat logs, Slack or ordinary email. ## Shared-hosting release pattern For Node apps that remain on constrained cPanel/MochaHost environments, use CI-built Linux artifacts and versioned releases: ``` releases/<commit-sha>/ CURRENT PREVIOUS shared/ ``` Deploy artifact → switch active release → health check → rollback on failure. ## Static/Vite deployments For client-only apps: - build in CI or a trusted development environment - deploy generated client artifacts only - do not publish `.env`, source secrets, private server code or development-only files to the public document root ## Health endpoints Every deployable backend should provide a lightweight health endpoint such as `/healthz` for promotion and rollback checks.

items.title: Identity and Multi-Site Standard
items.summary: TAKATAK may provide the preferred master identity/federation layer during a managed contract, but client websites/applications are independently transferable products.
items.search_text: # Identity and Multi-Site Standard ## Core rule TAKATAK may provide the preferred master identity/federation layer during a managed contract, but client websites/applications are independently transferable products. Identity integration must therefore be **federated and replaceable**, not captive. ## Recommended relationship during TAKATAK-managed operation ``` person → client-local subject/user ID → optional TAKATAK master identity mapping → organization/workspace relationship → product/client entitlement → client application ``` A client application should retain a stable local identity/reference for its own domain records even when login is federated through TAKATAK. Recommended mapping: ``` client_local_user_id ↕ optional takatak_master_identity_id ``` The TAKATAK mapping can support cross-service operations, CRM, agency workflows and shared login while the client-local identifier protects transferability. ## Allowed identity patterns Depending on the client/product and contract: 1. **Local auth + TAKATAK account linking** 2. **TAKATAK as OIDC/OAuth identity provider** with documented replacement/migration path 3. **Dual/federated identity** 4. **TAKATAK-only operational auth during contract**, only if the transfer package includes a tested path to replace it Do not claim an application is transfer-ready if removing TAKATAK Auth makes all customer/admin access impossible and no replacement path exists. ## Cross-product rule Client applications must not: - access the TAKATAK database directly from browser code; - rely on sibling client databases; - send passwords, private credentials or raw secrets in redirect URLs; - silently merge one client's identities/customer records into another client's data; - assume identity federation grants authorization to every TAKATAK or sibling resource. Use versioned server-side APIs/contracts, signed handoffs and explicit scopes. ## Identity ≠ authorization A shared identity means only that the same person can be resolved across authorized systems. It does not automatically grant: - access to another client; - access to another business/location; - access to TAKATAK internal data; - cross-client customer/lead visibility; - administrative permissions. Authorization remains resource-, organization-, business- and product-scoped. ## Telecom handoff model For TAKATAK ↔ MIMT, known shared identifiers may include: - `global_user_id` - `workspace_id` - `business_id` - `telecom_account_id` - `service_subscription_id` - `phone_number_id` The MIMT application must still preserve its own transferable operational records and a documented replacement/auth path. ## Entitlements and managed-service lifecycle Product/service access can be driven by server-side entitlement state during the contract. Recommended lifecycle: - `ACTIVE_MANAGED` - `PAYMENT_ATTENTION` - `SUSPENDED_BY_CONTRACT` - `TRANSFER_PENDING` - `TRANSFER_READY` - `TRANSFERRED` - `TERMINATED` Suspension must be auditable and reversible when the contract permits it. Do not destroy data or corrupt the client application as leverage. ## Transfer/offboarding identity requirements A transfer plan must identify: - client-local identities; - TAKATAK identity mappings; - account export/migration rules; - password reset or new identity-provider migration path; - client-owned vs TAKATAK-managed OAuth applications; - third-party reauthorization requirements; - session/token revocation; - credential rotation. For the broader transfer architecture, see `docs/11-CLIENT-INDEPENDENCE-TRANSFER-ARCHITECTURE.md`.

items.title: AI Agent Operating Rules
items.summary: Preferred tool division:
items.search_text: # AI Agent Operating Rules ## Roles in the TAKATAK workflow Preferred tool division: - GitHub: engineering source of truth - ChatGPT / Codex: architecture, implementation planning and code-oriented execution - Cursor: local/native execution and debugging - Claude: independent review, large-context inspection and secondary analysis - Lovable: exportable web UI and rapid visual/product implementation Production ownership remains with TAKATAK-controlled GitHub repositories, databases, domains and infrastructure. ## Required agent behavior Before building: 1. discover existing implementation, 2. reuse existing contracts/components where appropriate, 3. standardize cross-project patterns, 4. identify approval/security gates, 5. then build. Reusable sequence: **DISCOVER → REUSE → STANDARDIZE → APPROVE → BUILD** Agents must not: - fabricate integrations, - treat mock data as live, - disclose secrets, - bypass authorization boundaries, - silently duplicate existing systems, - overwrite a current architecture with an older historical decision without noting the conflict.

items.title: TAKATAK Cross-Project Design Preferences
items.summary: TAKATAK sites should feel intentionally designed, polished, modern and animated rather than like unmodified templates.
items.search_text: # TAKATAK Cross-Project Design Preferences ## Goal TAKATAK sites should feel intentionally designed, polished, modern and animated rather than like unmodified templates. ## Reusable visual direction Across projects, prioritize: - clean, sharp layouts - strong visual hierarchy - polished headers and hero sections - high-quality imagery - responsive cards and carousels - motion/transition polish - tasteful shifting/animated visual states - refined pop-up/modal experiences - mobile-first navigation - professional loading/empty/error states - consistent spacing and typography - strong call-to-action hierarchy ## Shared experience patterns When applicable, reusable site patterns may include: - TAKATAK OTP/login surfaces - sponsor/advertising placements - AdSense-compatible placements where appropriate - social links/connections - animated menus - promotional carousels - location/business cards - multilingual navigation - responsive dashboards ## Rule Visual work must not silently change domain logic, backend contracts or authorization rules. UI modernization is a separate concern from business logic unless a project explicitly combines both scopes. ## Lovable role Lovable is primarily useful for fast visual/product implementation and exportable UI. Production ownership and source-of-truth remain in TAKATAK-controlled GitHub/infrastructure.

items.title: Integration Standards
items.summary: Use official APIs, documented partner interfaces and authorized OAuth/account connections.
items.search_text: # Integration Standards ## Official integration rule Use official APIs, documented partner interfaces and authorized OAuth/account connections. Do not present mock or placeholder integrations as live. ## Provider checklist Before implementing a provider: 1. verify current official documentation, 2. confirm production access/approval requirements, 3. identify OAuth/scopes or API-key model, 4. define account/location mapping, 5. define webhook/event authority, 6. implement idempotency, 7. define retry and dead-letter behavior, 8. encrypt tokens at rest, 9. never expose provider secrets to browser code, 10. record audit/provenance for important state changes. ## Webhooks Webhook services should include: - signature verification - timestamp/replay validation where supported - idempotency keys/event IDs - deterministic tenant/location resolution - safe retry semantics - no secret/token logging ## External status Do not invent extra provider states to compensate for unclear UI. Normalize provider states into a small explicit internal model and retain the raw provider status separately for debugging/provenance. ## Live vs simulated Every integration surface should make it obvious whether data is: - live - sandbox/test - simulated/mock - stale/unavailable

items.search_text: # Client Independence, Managed Services and Transfer Architecture ## Core business requirement TAKATAK builds and operates client websites/applications during a managed contract, commonly with a long service horizon such as five years. The client platform must nevertheless remain a real, separable software product that can be transferred at the end of the applicable agreement. The architecture must therefore satisfy both goals: 1. **Independent client platform** — the client can ultimately receive the agreed application/code/assets/data package and run it without being forced to keep TAKATAK. 2. **TAKATAK managed engine** — during the contract, TAKATAK can supply identity federation, AI, advertising, lead generation, social, analytics, automation, messaging, billing, integrations and operational services through explicit interfaces. A client application is not a disposable frontend for TAKATAK. It is an independent product with optional/contracted TAKATAK services attached. ## Non-negotiable separation Every transferable client platform should have, where technically appropriate: - its own repository or clearly separable repository boundary; - its own domain(s); - its own environment configuration; - its own deployment manifest/runbook; - its own database/schema or exportable isolated tenant boundary; - its own application/business logic; - its own static/media assets that are part of the transfer package; - tests and release process; - an inventory of external dependencies; - an explicit TAKATAK adapter boundary. TAKATAK services must be consumed through versioned APIs, events, OAuth/federation, webhooks, SDK/adapters or documented connector contracts. Do not make a client platform depend on reading TAKATAK's production database directly. Do not make client applications call sibling client databases directly. ## Independence test A platform is transfer-ready only when an engineer can answer: > If the TAKATAK-managed connectors are disabled and the agreed replacement services are configured, can this application still be deployed, authenticated, operated and maintained as an independent product? If the answer is no, there is an architectural coupling defect to document. ## Identity model — federated, not captive During the managed contract, TAKATAK Auth may be the preferred login/identity provider. However, a transferable client application must not make its own continued existence impossible when the TAKATAK identity service is removed. Recommended model: ``` Client local subject / user ID ↕ optional federation mapping TAKATAK master identity ID ``` Store a stable local application identifier and, when connected, an optional immutable TAKATAK identity mapping. A transferable client app may use one of these patterns: - local auth plus TAKATAK account linking; - TAKATAK Auth as OIDC/OAuth identity provider with a documented replacement path; - dual/federated identity with migration/export tooling. Never store passwords in redirect URLs. Never require direct browser access to TAKATAK databases. ## Data classes Data transfer cannot be decided by one vague "customers belong to X" flag. Model provenance and rights explicitly. ### CLIENT_PLATFORM_DATA Application configuration, client content, catalog/menu, operational records and other data created inside the client's own software. Transfer treatment: governed by the contract and applicable law; normally part of the platform/offboarding package when it is the client's business data. ### CLIENT_FIRST_PARTY_DATA Customer/account/order/request data collected directly by the client platform from the client's own users/customers. Transfer treatment: must be handled according to the contract, privacy notices, consent, applicable law and processor/controller roles. Do not silently classify first-party customer records as TAKATAK property merely because TAKATAK operated the software. ### TAKATAK_AGENCY_DATA Examples: - TAKATAK-owned lead marketplace inventory; - agency prospecting lists; - cross-client campaign intelligence; - TAKATAK model/routing performance; - proprietary scoring; - internal optimization signals; - TAKATAK network audience/placement data; - internal prompts/workflows not sold as client deliverables; - provider cost/margin information; - internal operational analytics. Transfer treatment: excluded from a client software transfer when the contract and data/privacy basis permit. The client may receive results/deliverables without receiving the proprietary engine or cross-client dataset. ### TAKATAK_ORIGINATED_LEADS Leads supplied by the TAKATAK network/agency rather than organically created as the client's own first-party records must retain provenance. Required fields should include: - `lead_source` - `source_network` - `source_campaign_id` - `source_owner` - `client_license_scope` - `created_at` - `consent_basis` where applicable - `transfer_class` At offboarding, transferability follows the contract, user consent/privacy obligations and the lead-source agreement. Do not use hidden copying or undisclosed extraction. ### SHARED_DERIVED_DATA Reports/scores/segments derived from both client and TAKATAK data. Transfer treatment: define in the contract and metadata. Where practical, distinguish transferable client-facing output from TAKATAK's reusable methodology/model. ### CREDENTIALS_AND_SECRETS API keys, service-role keys, private signing keys, internal tokens and other secrets. Transfer treatment: never copy TAKATAK-owned provider credentials into a transfer. Client-owned credentials may be rotated/reissued to the client through a secure process. ### THIRD_PARTY_DATA Data governed by Meta, Google, Stripe, Twilio, Clover, delivery platforms, social networks, AI providers, etc. Transfer treatment: subject to the third party's terms and account ownership. Build reconnect/reauthorize paths rather than assuming credentials can be transferred. ## Managed-service boundary Client application: ``` CLIENT APP ├─ own UX ├─ own domain ├─ own business rules ├─ own data boundary ├─ own build/deploy package └─ TAKATAK adapters ↓ versioned APIs/events ↓ TAKATAK MANAGED SERVICES ├─ Auth/federation ├─ CRM/agency operations ├─ Leads ├─ Ads ├─ Social ├─ AI Nexus ├─ Automations ├─ Messaging ├─ Analytics ├─ Billing where contracted └─ Connector Vault / third-party integrations ``` The client app receives only the capabilities/data its contract and authorization allow. ## Commercial entitlement and suspension Do not implement destructive "hostage" mechanics, secret kill switches or data deletion as payment enforcement. Use explicit, auditable commercial states: - `TRIAL` - `ACTIVE_MANAGED` - `PAYMENT_ATTENTION` - `SUSPENDED_BY_CONTRACT` - `TRANSFER_PENDING` - `TRANSFER_READY` - `TRANSFERRED` - `TERMINATED` If the agreement permits suspension for non-payment, suspend managed services/access in a documented, reversible way. Preserve data according to retention obligations. Never corrupt code or destroy client records as leverage. ## Five-year / end-of-contract transfer package Where the contract provides for transfer, prepare a reproducible handoff containing the agreed scope: - source repository snapshot or transferred repo; - tagged release and commit SHA; - build instructions; - environment variable template with no secrets; - database/schema migrations; - agreed client-data export; - media/assets in scope; - third-party dependency inventory; - DNS/domain handoff instructions where applicable; - deployment runbook; - backup/restore runbook; - tests and known limitations; - admin/user documentation; - replacement instructions for TAKATAK-managed connectors; - list of services/features that will stop when TAKATAK is disconnected; - credential rotation checklist; - final acceptance record. TAKATAK proprietary platform code, cross-client datasets, internal AI/routing systems and agency-owned lead inventory are not included unless the contract explicitly includes them. ## Client adapter rule Every TAKATAK integration should have a narrow interface, for example: ``` IdentityAdapter LeadProviderAdapter AiGenerationAdapter SocialPublishingAdapter AdsAdapter MessagingAdapter AnalyticsAdapter BillingAdapter ReviewAdapter CommerceConnectorAdapter ``` The client-specific application calls the interface; the TAKATAK implementation can later be replaced. ## Repository rule A client repository may contain: - adapter contracts; - local domain logic; - UI; - tests; - mock/test implementations; - environment variable names; - migration/export tools. It must not contain: - TAKATAK master API secrets; - reusable cross-client lead databases; - private agency intelligence; - unrestricted service-role credentials; - secrets belonging to another client. ## Audit requirement For every client platform, add a `TRANSFERABILITY.md` or equivalent document answering: - What does the client receive? - What remains TAKATAK intellectual property/service? - Which data classes exist? - Which domains/accounts are client-owned vs TAKATAK-managed? - Which third-party accounts must be reauthorized? - Which features fail when TAKATAK is disconnected? - What replacement adapters are required? - What is the current transfer-readiness status? ## Contract alignment warning Technical metadata should represent the signed agreement; it must not silently invent ownership rights. Any ambiguous customer/lead ownership, privacy role, retention right, or transfer exclusion must be marked `LEGAL/CONTRACT REVIEW REQUIRED` rather than guessed by code or AI.

The 2026 cleanup starts from `docs/10-PORTFOLIO-DOMAINS-REPOS-2026-10-06.md`, but the final truth must come from live registrar, DNS, hosting, GitHub and deployment evidence. ## Cleanup sequence ### A. Domain/hosting reconciliation Export the current domain/account list from MochaHost/cPanel and any other registrar/host. For each domain: - verify registration status and expiration; - identify registrar; - identify authoritative nameservers/DNS provider; - identify current A/AAAA/CNAME/MX records; - identify SSL state; - identify hosting account/document root; - identify whether WordPress, static, Node, redirect, parked or unused; - identify client/business; - identify canonical domain and redirects. Do not delete or let a domain lapse solely because it is not mapped yet. ### B. GitHub reconciliation For every repository: - identify project/business; - identify canonical domain; - determine current/legacy/experimental status; - determine default and production branch; - inspect secrets exposure and committed `.env` files; - identify CI/CD; - identify deployment target; - identify live database/storage; - identify owner/maintainer; - add a README where missing; - add transferability metadata for client projects. ### C. Deployment reconciliation Build a deployment registry: - Contabo/Coolify - MochaHost/cPanel/Passenger/WordPress - Vercel - Lovable-hosted preview/production - Supabase Edge/runtime where relevant - Cloudflare DNS/proxy - other providers Every production service gets: - health check - deployment source - rollback path - backup path - last verified date ### D. Client contract boundary For each client: - platform/code transfer terms; - contract start/end; - hosting responsibility; - domain ownership/management; - data classes; - first-party customer-data treatment; - TAKATAK-originated lead treatment; - third-party account ownership; - offboarding package; - payment/suspension rules; - transfer readiness. ### E. Marketing/account reconciliation Map: - Meta Business / ad account - Google Ads - Search Console - GA4 - Google Business Profile - TikTok/YouTube/LinkedIn/etc. - email sender domains - Twilio numbers/messaging - Stripe/Clover/delivery platform connections to the correct project/client. ### F. Archive / retire A project can be marked `RETIRED` only after: - ownership/contract is known; - source is backed up/tagged; - data retention is handled; - DNS/email impact is checked; - replacement/redirect is documented; - client approval is recorded where required. ## Required statuses Use one of: `ACTIVE_PRODUCTION` `ACTIVE_MANAGED` `STAGING` `BUILDING` `PLANNED` `DORMANT` `LEGACY` `TRANSFER_PENDING` `TRANSFER_READY` `TRANSFERRED` `RETIRED` `UNKNOWN_NEEDS_AUDIT` ## Deliverables The cleanup is complete when there is: 1. a domain registry, 2. a repository registry, 3. a deployment registry, 4. a client/contract map, 5. a data-rights/offboarding map, 6. a provider/account registry, 7. a list of duplicates/legacy assets, 8. a prioritized 90-day work plan. Do not equate "not found in GitHub" with "not real." WordPress/cPanel sites and unpublished domains may exist without a dedicated repository.

items.search_text: # Engineering decisions — knowledgeAI ## 2026-10-14 — public catalog vs private knowledge **Decision:** Keep GitHub and Vercel catalogs strictly PUBLIC, based solely on allowlisted Markdown already in this public repository. Use a read-only search API and explicit \`visibility: public\` response metadata. **Reason:** This repo is publicly visible; public static assets and serverless code cannot be a confidential cross-tenant knowledge store. A privileged search endpoint without verified TAKATAK Auth could expose customer records. **Consequence:** Real private ingestion and retrieval require a separate authorized backend with durable storage, secrets off-Git, tenant and product claims enforced server-side, provenance and audit controls. ## 2026-10-14 — runtime and release chain **Decision:** Keep the existing Vercel project and static portal; add minimal JavaScript serverless API routes with no runtime dependencies. Python standard library remains responsible for the deterministic index. Node's built-in test runner validates APIs in CI. **Reason:** Reuse an existing deployment, avoid unnecessary framework migration, and preserve fast static navigation. ## Earlier documented decisions (still valid) - TAKATAK shared identity is federated; independent clients retain transferable local domain data: \`docs/05-IDENTITY-AND-MULTISITE.md\`. - Deployment security gates are mandatory; broken CI must not knowingly be promoted: \`docs/04-DEPLOYMENT-STANDARDS.md\`. - The public GitHub corpus cannot contain confidential personal/professional messages or keys: \`README.md\`, \`docs/03-INGESTION-POLICY.md\`. - Agent and provider integrations must not be presented as live without actual production evidence: \`docs/06-AGENT-OPERATING-RULES.md\`. When production evidence contradicts this log, record the conflict and do not silently overwrite earlier history. ## 2026-10-14 — production HTTP evidence **Decision:** Require an independent GitHub-hosted HTTP smoke check after publishing the catalog. This verifies real HTTPS for the portal, JSON catalog, health probe and read-only agent search, beyond Vercel's READY indicator. Successful evidence: GitHub run `38623184283`. Keep production SHA checks separate because Vercel can automatically deploy before a CI job completes. ## 2026-10-14 — no false OIDC/JWKS integration The accessible TAKATAK core code uses Supabase sessions and database-backed workspace permission checks. Its publicly found `/.well-known/jwks.json` is a **Bluesky provider key**, not a TAKATAK identity federation contract. KnowledgeAI must obtain a real approved signed service token or secure server-to-server authority before private data access. See `docs/PRIVATE-AUTH-CONTRACT.md`. ## 2026-10-14 — safe concurrent catalog generation Multiple agents may change `main` while GitHub Actions generates its public search index. The bot must not publish a stale snapshot or force-overwrite another agent. It re-fetches the current `main`, regenerates the index from that version, and uses bounded retries for a regular Git push. A rejected race is reported rather than bypassed. ## 2026-10-14 — isolated private-service code, no public data plane Implemented a standalone private-knowledge service and RLS schema behind a dedicated RS256 JWT contract with audience, issuer, product, workspace and explicit read/write scopes. No private credentials or tenant data are held in this public repository. The service is not deployed while the TAKATAK issuer, separate PostgreSQL instance and operational controls are unverified. CI uses synthetic identities and a disposable PostgreSQL 17 container. ## 2026-10-14 — reproducibility and private integration proof Use pinned pg dependency plus committed package-lock.json and npm ci; fail CI on npm audit findings at high severity or above. Test the private app, not just its SQL migration, against a disposable PostgreSQL 17 with restricted runtime login. The tests prove implementation behavior but do not grant approval to load confidential source material or deploy without real TAKATAK authorization. ## 2026-10-14 — tenant-only deletion with audit-preserving lifecycle Permit knowledge:read to list only current source metadata; require a separate knowledge:delete authorization for irreversible deletion of all source versions. Both operations resolve workspace from verified signed claims and use database RLS. Keep audit metadata and anti-replay receipts outside deletion until a documented retention/offboarding policy is approved. Limit list results at the database and reject repeated or missing source IDs. Private CI proves cross-tenant isolation and audits as the migration owner without granting audit read privileges to the runtime login. ## 2026-10-14 — explicit private source portability scope Provide full original source revisions only with a separate signed `knowledge:export` scope; never elevate a standard `knowledge:read` token to bulk export. Enforce workspace filtering through PostgreSQL RLS, SQL pagination capped at ten revisions, no cache and metadata-only audit. All related operations remain in the undeployed private service pending a verified TAKATAK identity/entitlement authority. ## 2026-10-14 — tenant pagination before export Support deterministic ordered, bounded source inventory pages with SQL LIMIT/OFFSET and explicit validated maximums. Workspace comes exclusively from validated signed identity and PostgreSQL RLS, not a request parameter. This makes source version export complete without broadening the public catalog or exposing cross-tenant source names. ## 2026-10-15 — refuse stale or self-assigned private access Require an independent database authorization row on **every** private operation, in addition to verifying the RSA-signed token and operation scope. New workspaces default disabled and permissions default false; JWTs can be revoked by `workspace_id` + `jti`. The app role receives SELECT-only access to these tables and cannot issue/revoke credentials or change workspace entitlements. The trusted TAKATAK master remains the sole source of identity, membership and product authorization. Do not invent a second login authority in KnowledgeAI. ## 2026-10-15 — private startup fail-closed Before binding a private HTTP listener, verify runtime SQL login is not a superuser/BYPASSRLS/table owner; require every expected table to FORCE RLS, forbid runtime mutation of access controls, forbid runtime audit reads, and require PostgreSQL TLS. CI may bypass TLS **only** in a disposable local test of the preflight; production code does not expose such an override. ## 2026-10-15 — no TLS downgrade through database URL Reject PostgreSQL DSN query options that could replace the pinned Node TLS peer-verification object. Keep strict certificate verification and require approved private trust configuration. Production private DB bootstrap must fail when connection encryption or authorization constraints are inadequate. ## 2026-10-15 — restore-integrity evidence before private rollout Adopt a synthetic, disposable PostgreSQL backup/restore drill in CI. Require recovered FORCE RLS, correct tenant records, deletion state, audit, disabled-workspace entitlements and revoked-token records. Use no live customer content in CI; never publish backup artifacts. A passing CI is not evidence of encrypted offsite production backup, retention, WAL/PITR or an agreed RPO/RTO. ## 2026-10-15 — durable quota counters instead of process-local counters Use per-workspace, per-operation, per-minute PostgreSQL counters with transactional UPSERT and FORCE RLS so separate private backend instances share the same limit. Do not accept tenant, permission or limit values from browser query parameters. Exceeded quotas throw 429 before protected reads or writes; the containing transaction rolls back. Hard-coded limits are abuse controls, not billing meters or a substitute for gateway-level throttling. Bucket retention and production alerting remain separately governed work. ## 2026-10-15 — deny-by-default privileged retention Implement an unscheduled operator-only SQL maintenance script, not an API. Default to a non-destructive preview. Require explicit opt-in and independently authorized database credentials before bounded deletion of historical rate buckets, expired anti-replay receipts and revoked JWTs long after expiry. Never allow the KnowledgeAI private runtime SQL role to run cleanup; never delete documents, audit logs or workspace entitlements from this operation. Expiry bounds used in synthetic tests are not substitutes for approved production retention and legal-hold policies. ## 2026-10-15 — explicit provenance approval, not arbitrary HTTPS ingestion Signed write scopes and company entitlements alone do not grant authority to ingest arbitrary external or private documents. Require a separate admin-managed and expiring approval for the exact source ID and HTTPS URL inside the verified workspace; do not allow API runtime to edit approvals. The seven-table FORCE RLS preflight and staging restore checks now cover approval metadata. Removal of already stored versions remains an independent audited delete/retention operation; revoking an ingestion approval does not implicitly erase historical versions. ## 2026-10-15 — bridge via TAKATAK rather than creating identity authority Keep TAKATAK as the unique user/workspace authority. Publish a reusable pure Node RS256 KnowledgeAI token/JWKS emitter that accepts only server-resolved `client_scoped` access plus two independent trusted callbacks: verified KnowledgeAI product entitlement and requested-scope authorization. Never create credentials, login pages or browser-controlled role grants inside KnowledgeAI. Dedicated RSA keys remain external, short-lived operation-scoped JWTs last 60 seconds, and the already-isolated private service revalidates database entitlements and revocation. Without an actual TAKATAK product grant or issuer route, production stays disabled. ## TAKATAK integration checkpoint 2026-10-16: central master TAKATAK is the only KnowledgeAI user/organization authority. Dedicated default-off KnowledgeAiGrant rows control separate read/write/delete/export scopes in draft master PR #194; JWT signing remains server-only. Existing public KnowledgeAI Vercel content stays separate. ## 2026-10-16 — master-owned, disabled-by-default private search proxy Prefer a TAKATAK-server-to-KnowledgeAI-backend read proxy rather than returning private JWTs to browser code. Gate on a current TAKATAK session, active company/profile/membership, active KnowledgeAI catalog product, and an explicitly enabled nonexpired profile+workspace+scope grant. Never inherit unrelated `ai_studio`, admin or demo permissions. Master PR #195 adds the code behind `TAKATAK_KNOWLEDGEAI_ENABLED=1`; no migration/grant/signing key is active yet. Independent KnowledgeAI private DB still validates its own seven-table RLS, entitlements, token revocation and source approvals. ## 2026-10-16 — no parallel KnowledgeAI identity contracts Protect TAKATAK as the sole customer and workspace authority. Two master drafts currently implement incompatible entitlements: PR #194 (`knowledgeai_grants`) and #195 (`knowledgeai_workspace_grants`). These must be reconciled into ONE approved schema/signing interface before any merge or provisioning. For any browser-facing private knowledge proxy, require fresh Supabase `getUser()` authentication (high-risk route), validated master per-user/per-company grant, fixed scope and server-only JWT; do not rely on a cached session or return the bearer to the browser. No production activation or auto-merge is permitted until a real two-company test and dedicated secured backend are verified.

items.search_text: # Deployment runbook — knowledgeAI ## Verified topology (2026-10-14) - Repository: \`https://github.com/takatakca/knowledgeAI\` (public), publication branch: \`main\`. - Portal: Git-linked Vercel project \`knowledgeai\`. - Production alias: \`https://knowledgeai-nu.vercel.app\`. - Vercel production deployment for SHA `4ca3ad226a56a3df0fb5fe88e090f723c5821ffe` was **READY** and external GitHub runner HTTP smoke verified four routes on 2026-10-14 (GitHub Actions run `38623184283`). - GitHub Actions \`Knowledge Catalog CI\` runs Python tests, builds catalog and publishes refreshed \`knowledge-catalog.json\` to \`main\`. - Vercel may create two releases per content change: the author's commit and the catalog bot commit. ## Deploy and smoke checks 1. Push authorized, reviewed changes to \`main\` (never force-push). 2. Open GitHub **Actions → Knowledge Catalog CI**. Require successful unit tests and index generation. 3. GitHub CI now includes an automatic external HTTPS smoke job after catalog publishing. Check it passed; if it fails, fix Vercel routes/domain/authorization before claiming production. Check whether the catalog bot pushed a follow-up commit; use its SHA as the final production target. 4. Inspect the \`knowledgeai\` project on Vercel; verify \`READY\` **and** \`githubCommitSha\` matches the target branch. 5. From an external browser or curl, verify: \`\`\`sh curl -i https://knowledgeai-nu.vercel.app/ curl -i https://knowledgeai-nu.vercel.app/knowledge-catalog.json curl -i https://knowledgeai-nu.vercel.app/api/health curl -i 'https://knowledgeai-nu.vercel.app/api/search?q=TAKATAK&limit=3' curl -i -X POST https://knowledgeai-nu.vercel.app/api/search \`\`\` Expect HTML 200; catalog JSON version 1; health JSON 200 \`status=ok\`; search JSON 200 with real source URLs; POST 405. 6. If Vercel returns READY but external access fails, diagnose routing/domain/SSO/dns before declaring public release successful. 7. When reversing code, restore a known-good Git commit, let GitHub/Vercel redeploy and verify the final alias; do not force-push. ## CI commands (local) \`\`\`sh python3 -m unittest discover -s ingest/tests -v python3 ingest/build_catalog.py python3 ingest/build_catalog.py --check node --test tests/public-api.test.cjs node --check api/search.js node --check api/health.js \`\`\` ## Non-public AI Studio \`deploy/ai-studio/\` is a separate VPS kit, **not deployed by Vercel**. Follow its existing runbook only after server/DNS/API-keys and costs are approved. Never commit \`.env\`, passwords or downloaded client data. ## Concurrency recovery (verified 2026-10-14) Parallel source edits can race with the catalog bot. The publish job now fetches the latest `main`, resets **only its ephemeral runner checkout**, regenerates `knowledge-catalog.json`, and retries a normal push. No force-push or destructive remote reset is used. If retries exhaust, inspect GitHub logs and re-run only after reconciling newer source changes. Verified successful production smoke after this fix: GitHub Actions run `38623893521`. ## Private backend — separate non-public deployment Do not deploy private-knowledge/ to Vercel public portal. It is a future isolated server, requiring the approved credential issuer, dedicated private PostgreSQL instance, RLS runtime role, secure network/proxy and backup/retention. Current evidence is synthetic JWT unit tests and a disposable PostgreSQL 17 RLS CI test. The service does not claim production availability. See private-knowledge/README.md. ## Latest reproducible private-service security checks CI run 38627614637 succeeded. The separate Private Knowledge Security CI checks JWT verifier syntax/tests, PostgreSQL 17 migration and FORCE RLS, cross-tenant restricted-role ingestion/search, replay denial, deterministic npm ci using private-knowledge/package-lock.json, and npm audit of production packages at high severity threshold. The private service is STILL NOT deployed; Vercel is only for the public corpus/API. ## Private lifecycle migration 002 After applying migration 001 in a separately approved private PostgreSQL DB, apply `private-knowledge/migrations/002_source_lifecycle.sql`. Provision the restricted runtime role with SELECT/INSERT/DELETE on documents, SELECT/INSERT on write_receipts, INSERT on audit (not SELECT), plus sequence and schema permissions. Verify all tenant cross-access tests. There is **no automatic private production deployment**; public Vercel remains a separate read-only service. Evidence: Private Knowledge Security CI run 38629828659. ## New private export migration (2026-10-14) Apply `private-knowledge/migrations/003_export_audit.sql` after 001 and 002. Export is served only by the isolated private server, using `knowledge:export`, 10-version maximum pagination and audit. CI run `38630318645` passes synthetic two-tenant export isolation; **there is no production deployment** for this API. Public Vercel remains independent and cannot access confidential records. ## Source pagination validation Latest private CI run `38630925562` verified SQL-bounded inventory pagination with restricted PostgreSQL roles and source export. Do NOT publish this private API to the public Vercel site. Migration prerequisites remain 001→002→003 and confidential TAKATAK-authenticated service infrastructure. ## 2026-10-15 — migration 004 and private startup gate 1. Apply **001 → 002 → 003 → 004** in a dedicated approved private PostgreSQL as migration owner. Never apply private migrations to unrelated TAKATAK/customer projects. 2. The authorized TAKATAK backend or its privileged database operator must explicitly insert/update `workspace_entitlements` for each verified active workspace. All booleans default false. To revoke a particular still-valid JWT, write its `workspace_id`, `jti` and expiration into `revoked_tokens` from a trusted control-plane identity. Never expose these admin writes to the normal service role. 3. Grant the distinct non-owner runtime login SELECT only on `workspace_entitlements` and `revoked_tokens`; allow only previously documented tenant RLS data access, and INSERT-only on audit. 4. Before HTTP bind, private `assertDatabaseSafety()` now rejects privileged ownership, RLS not forced, unsafe SQL grants, or PostgreSQL plaintext sessions. Configure a verified TLS CA through protected host settings. Startup must fail if configuration is not ready. 5. Tests: `node --test private-knowledge/tests/private.test.cjs private-knowledge/tests/access.test.cjs private-knowledge/tests/preflight.test.cjs`; the Private Knowledge Security CI runs a disposable PostgreSQL instance and live restricted-role checks. 6. Actual private deployment remains unapproved and unconfigured. Vercel must continue serving only the public knowledge catalog. ## PostgreSQL DSN TLS safety — 2026-10-15 Private startup now rejects URLs containing `sslmode`, `sslcert`, `sslkey`, `sslrootcert` or `ssl` parameters, because database connection-string parsing can override the strict TLS settings on the Node PostgreSQL client. Supply a clean `postgresql://` connection URL via protected secrets and configure a trusted CA at the host TLS trust layer when necessary; never set `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0`. CI tests these rejection cases. Private production is still NOT DEPLOYED. ## 2026-10-15 — private disaster-recovery gate The separate Private Knowledge Security CI now verifies a full disposable PostgreSQL archive restore, including RLS and tenant authorization state. Evidence: GitHub Actions run 38801324564. The synthetic archive is deleted after CI and never uploaded. See `docs/PRIVATE-RECOVERY.md`. No production backup service, offsite storage or retention schedule is configured. Do not deploy the private backend before the authorized independent database and its protected recovery plan are genuinely operational. ## 2026-10-15 — migration 005, private request quotas Apply migrations **001 → 002 → 003 → 004 → 005** in a dedicated approved confidential PostgreSQL instance, using the migration owner. Grant the non-owner app role SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE only on `knowledge_private.request_windows`; never DELETE or BYPASSRLS. The startup preflight now requires **six** FORCE RLS tables and appropriate quota-table grants. `private-knowledge/src/rate-limit.cjs` enforces read=120, write=30, delete=20 and export=30 requests per workspace/minute. When the limit is exhausted, the API returns HTTP 429 and rolls back its transaction. Quota buckets are not automatically purged; a privileged retention plan is required before live activation. The network gateway should rate-limit unauthenticated traffic separately. Evidence: private CI 38802621695. **The private service remains undeployed; Vercel hosts only public content.** ## 2026-10-15 — manual retention, not scheduled See `docs/PRIVATE-RETENTION.md` and `private-knowledge/maintenance/retention.sql`. The script previews old operational-row counts without writing by default. An authorized operator may execute bounded cleanup only with both `apply=true` and `approved=true`; privileges and legal approval remain external prerequisites. Synthetic PostgreSQL regression CI passed (`38839681826`). No production cleanup task or backup-retention schedule was enabled. Audit and customer documents are not in cleanup scope. ## 2026-10-15 — private migration 006 approval gate Apply migrations **001 → 002 → 003 → 004 → 005 → 006** as an approved migration owner on the independent private database only. The regular KnowledgeAI runtime role requires SELECT, but never write privileges, on `knowledge_private.source_approvals`. Startup preflight requires its seventh FORCE RLS table, safe grants and a protected TLS connection. A trusted TAKATAK operator must separately manage source approval, expiry and confidentiality classifications, never via an unauthenticated client form. Verify synthetic tests in CI, then real staging denial cases and restore. See `docs/PRIVATE-SOURCE-APPROVALS.md`. No live private deployment has occurred. ## 2026-10-15 — TAKATAK issuer contract, not deployed The portable signing library `private-knowledge/integrations/takatak-issuer.cjs` was tested with synthetic TAKATAK-style active workspace access and validates with the existing private KnowledgeAI RS256 verifier. It is deliberately not imported by public Vercel code or exposed through an HTTP route. See `docs/TAKATAK-ISSUER-INTEGRATION.md` for exact server-only callback, secrets/JWKS, approved product entitlement and scope mapping prerequisites. Production private deployment remains blocked on dedicated DB, signer, encrypted backups and staging verification; do not flip flags without evidence. ## TAKATAK integration checkpoint 2026-10-16: TAKATAK PR #194 is UNMERGED and off by default. Do not assume the master issuer exists in production. On approval, validate migration, protected signing config, real membership/product scope rights, JWKS, independent private KnowledgeAI PostgreSQL TLS/RLS and backup drills before launch. ## 2026-10-16 — TAKATAK bridge release gate [Draft TAKATAK PR #195](https://github.com/takatakca/takatak-v1/pull/195) carries the proposed master integration. It is OFF by default and NOT merged. The master needs coordinator PR review/CI and an approved database migration for `knowledgeai_workspace_grants`; no grants, `ProductCatalog` activation, secrets or user sessions are generated by the migration. Server secret names: `TAKATAK_KNOWLEDGEAI_ENABLED`, `TAKATAK_KNOWLEDGEAI_ISSUER`, `TAKATAK_KNOWLEDGEAI_AUDIENCE`, `TAKATAK_KNOWLEDGEAI_KID`, `TAKATAK_KNOWLEDGEAI_SIGNING_KEY_PEM`, `TAKATAK_KNOWLEDGEAI_PRIVATE_ORIGIN`. Only after separately approved private KnowledgeAI DB/JWKS/TLS and multi-tenant checks should an administrator enable the integration. The master proxy returns search results only, not a signing token. Vercel public catalog is NOT the confidential gateway. ## 2026-10-16 — reviewed CI and master merge blocker TAKATAK PR #195 baseline `c4e2ee001ebf5d2be8d1e1403aac83e2ccfaf18c` completed master CI run [38884205088](https://github.com/takatakca/takatak-v1/actions/runs/38884205088) successfully. The follow-up high-risk-route source commit `5f76e0bee202162c9569b01ef0f52372211ab98b` and worklog commit `3bd6c1ef0bb6b2a49dd27325c37c600e907fae80` require fresh CI confirmation. PR #194 is an incompatible overlapping draft; coordinator MUST choose a single master grant table and JWKS issuer, not merge both SQL migrations. No signing keys, grants, private deployment, customer data, paid Supabase projects or migrations were provisioned by this work. Vercel READY is PUBLIC only; continue staging checks against a separately authorized confidential backend.

items.search_text: # Private KnowledgeAI Auth integration — VERIFIED discovery, not live Date: **2026-10-14**. Source: public `takatakca/takatak-v1`, code revision `dcd454e42e95f08c407c53ab1af73ee2b36e0e4f`. ## Verified architecture evidence - `src/lib/auth/otp/session.ts`: TAKATAK uses Supabase SSR sessions and OTP/magic-link flows server-side; session management is not a generic bearer-token issue endpoint for downstream apps. - `src/lib/security/workspace-api.ts`: `requireWorkspaceApiPermission(permission)` derives access through `getServerAccessContext()` and `hasEffectivePermission()`; it distinguishes unauthenticated (401), missing workspace or permission (403), and unavailable DB/foundation demo (503). Only `client_scoped` access with permission is accepted. - `src/lib/security/workspace-guard.ts`: server-side permission checks on the selected workspace; identity alone is not authorization. - `src/app/.well-known/jwks.json/route.ts`: calls `getBlueskyPublicJwks()`. **It is for Bluesky OAuth, not a general TAKATAK identity issuer**. Do not use this endpoint to validate private KnowledgeAI access tokens. - `src/lib/integrations/facturations/service-token.ts`: verified example of a short-lived, service-specific JWT with `iss`, `aud`, `sub`, `business_id`, `roles`, `iat`, `exp`, `jti`; uses HS256 with a dedicated integration secret and a lifetime capped at 90 seconds. **Do not reuse Facturations' secret, audience or role claims for KnowledgeAI**. ## Proposed next boundary (NOT YET IMPLEMENTED) A TAKATAK-controlled server should: 1. authenticate a real Supabase session (or approved federation credential); 2. resolve workspace membership, active status, product entitlement and resource permission from authoritative server-side state; 3. issue a short-lived **KnowledgeAI-specific** service credential or call a private backend directly, with explicit issuer/audience, subject, workspace, product and least-privilege scope; 4. keep credentials and private source content off the browser, URLs, logs and this public GitHub repository; 5. maintain auditable tenant-scoped reads/writes and replay protection for ingestion jobs; 6. document private storage retention, deletion/transfer and reauthorization. A KnowledgeAI backend must reject tokens unless their cryptographic signature, issuer, audience, expiry, explicit scopes and authoritative workspace/entitlements have been verified. Never accept editable browser metadata, client-supplied `workspace_id` alone, a public repository search result or a valid login as sufficient authorization. ## Required external prerequisites - Explicit TAKATAK ↔ KnowledgeAI **private service contract** (how a real signed token is issued and validated), not merely a JWKS URL guessed from route names. - Approved database with tenant isolation and secure connection, encryption/backup/retention controls. - Approved classification of confidential source material and ingesting parties' permissions. - Separate private deployment with logging/monitoring and tests for both correct access and cross-client denial. Keep `/api/search` and `/api/health` PUBLIC and read-only. Do not expose a "private API" route until it has an actual authentication and storage implementation. ## 2026-10-14 — isolated implementation checkpoint The separate private-knowledge/ package now implements an RS256-only JWT verifier and RLS-backed PostgreSQL service with synthetic Node and PostgreSQL 17 isolation tests. The trusted TAKATAK token issuer, actual authorization mapping, approved private database, secrets and runtime remain NOT CONFIGURED. No routes were added to the public Vercel site. See private-knowledge/README.md.

items.search_text: # KnowledgeAI — private PostgreSQL recovery Status: **synthetic PostgreSQL restore rehearsal verified in CI (2026-10-15)**. **No production backup storage, encryption keys, remote retention or RPO/RTO are configured.** ## What is actually tested Private Knowledge Security CI uses PostgreSQL 17 with synthetic two-tenant fixtures. After the authenticated API tests, the workflow generates a custom-format archive with `pg_dump -Fc`, restores it into a second disposable database with `pg_restore --no-owner --exit-on-error`, then executes `private-knowledge/tests/restore.sql` as the schema owner and tenant-scoped queries as the restricted application role. The restore regression verifies: - Five private tables retain FORCE RLS, with runtime access limited by workspace. - Existing tenant A and tenant B records are restored in their own scope. - Previously deleted source revisions do not reappear after recovery. - Revoked JWTs, disabled entitlements and audit events remain present. - PostgreSQL tenant-scoped runtime grants still operate after recovery. - The temporary archive is deleted and is never committed or uploaded. ## Still required for production 1. Approve an independent confidential PostgreSQL database and authorized backup operator. 2. Configure encrypted offsite copies, independently protected keys and WAL/PITR. 3. Approve recovery-point, recovery-time, retention, deletion and legal-hold policies. 4. Repeat a real restoration drill in an isolated private environment with proper migration owner/runtime role separation, TLS and cross-company denial checks. 5. Document restoration evidence privately (archive identity, date, migrations, measured RPO/RTO, integrity evidence) without exposing customer data in GitHub. 6. Ensure deleted customer data ages out of snapshots according to approved policy. ## Local disposable CI equivalent ```sh pg_dump -U postgres -d knowledgeci -Fc > knowledge-private-rehearsal.dump createdb -U postgres knowledge_restore_ci pg_restore -U postgres -d knowledge_restore_ci --no-owner --exit-on-error < knowledge-private-rehearsal.dump psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U postgres -d knowledge_restore_ci -f private-knowledge/tests/restore.sql ``` These commands operate on **synthetic fixtures only**. They are NOT a production backup recipe: they lack encryption, offsite replication, scheduler, retention and recovery-authority controls. ## Extension: durable quota state The 2026-10-15 private security pipeline also verifies that the sixth FORCE RLS table, `request_windows`, and its tenant-scoped request counters survive the disposable PostgreSQL backup/restore round trip. This does not constitute a production backup, retention schedule or operational recovery guarantee.

items.search_text: # Private KnowledgeAI — operational retention preview **Status (2026-10-15): tested only with synthetic PostgreSQL 17 fixtures. Not scheduled or approved for live data.** ## Boundaries This operational maintenance command is not an HTTP route, is not available to clients and must never use the normal KnowledgeAI service role. It requires a separately approved privileged database operator and manual sign-off. The maintenance policy in the script supplies conservative **test thresholds**, which must be reviewed against actual legal, business and contractual retention rules before any production use: - Quota request windows: older than 48 hours. - Write anti-replay receipts: older than 24 hours (service JWTs expire within 5 minutes). - Revoked JWT records: more than 24 hours **after token expiration**. - Audit trail, documents, entitlements and backup archives: **never deleted by this command**. Each successful invocation deletes at most 500 eligible rows **per table**. It refuses concurrent execution through a transaction advisory lock. ## Preview-first operation Review privileged roles, retention policy and backups before use. The normal preview is non-destructive: ```sh psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f private-knowledge/maintenance/retention.sql ``` Applying a bounded batch requires both opt-in flags and an authorized DB operator: ```sh psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -v apply=true -v approved=true -f private-knowledge/maintenance/retention.sql ``` The flags are procedural safeguards, **not authentication or legal approval**. Database privileges determine which operators may run it. A failed invocation rolls back and must be investigated rather than bypassed. ## Evidence and non-goals Private Knowledge Security CI run `38839681826` verified default preview, explicit rejection without approval, deletion of only aged synthetic rows, and preservation of recent receipts/revocations, tenant documents, audit and entitlements. These are test fixtures rather than actual customer records. This command does **not** clean audit records, run on a schedule, implement right-to-erasure, manage legal holds, delete backups or guarantee offsite recovery. An independent approved operations workflow and private audit of each run are still required before deployment.

items.search_text: # Confidential source approval gate — KnowledgeAI **Status:** Implemented and tested with synthetic data in a disposable PostgreSQL 17 database. **NOT LIVE.** ## What the private service now checks Before accepting an upload, the service verifies a signed `knowledge:write` JWT, the current active workspace entitlement, token revocation, quota, and then an **independent approval record** for the exact authenticated workspace, `source_id` and HTTPS `source_url`. The approval must be explicitly enabled, already in effect and not expired. Missing, revoked, mismatched and expired approvals return HTTP 403 and cause the transaction to roll back. `source_approvals` is a new FORCE RLS table in migration `private-knowledge/migrations/006_source_approvals.sql`. Each row contains `workspace_id`, `source_id`, `source_url`, `classification` (`public`, `internal`, `restricted`), `approved`, `approved_by`, `approved_at`, and `expires_at`. The normal API SQL role has **SELECT only**; it cannot grant approval, alter classifications or extend expiration. ## Authority and operational boundary Only a trusted TAKATAK administrative control plane or separately authorized DB operator may create/revoke approvals, after verifying source ownership, right to process, confidentiality classification, active client consent and the correct workspace. This project does NOT implement that control plane. Never accept an `approved` field or classification from an unauthenticated web form as authorization. Do not copy real source contents into this public GitHub repository or into the public Vercel catalog. Revoking approval blocks **new ingestion** immediately. Previously stored source versions are not implicitly erased: removal requires the separate `knowledge:delete` operation and applicable retention, backups and legal-hold procedures. Never treat this approval table as a substitute for deletion. ## Deployment and verification 1. Provision the separately approved confidential PostgreSQL database, migration owner, non-owner service login and TLS trust. 2. Apply migrations 001 → 002 → 003 → 004 → 005 → **006**. 3. Grant the service role SELECT on `knowledge_private.source_approvals`. No INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE permissions to the HTTP service role. 4. Verify actual TAKATAK-issued JWT/entitlement contract and admin source approval workflow. Do not seed production rows from CI fixtures. 5. Check tests for missing, disabled, expired, wrong-workspace, wrong-URL and approved sources; run staging restore and check persisted approvals. 6. Only then consider deploying the private backend behind its protected network/gateway with auditing, backups and retention. CI synthetic fixtures are in `private-knowledge/tests/access-controls.sql`. `private-knowledge/tests/postgres.integration.test.cjs` exercises ingestion denials and success. `private-knowledge/tests/rls.sql` proves tenant-level read isolation and that a runtime login cannot self-approve. The restore test verifies approval metadata survives a full disposable database restore. ## Known limitations - Classification labels require an approved governance policy and reviewer. - This gate validates approval metadata; it is not malware, PII or secret scanning. - The service does not fetch the URL; it stores provenance supplied by an authorized caller. The trusted control plane must validate actual source rights. - A real provider/credential issuer, secret manager and private deployment remain unavailable and have not been simulated as live.

items.search_text: # KnowledgeAI public agent search API **Status:** deployed through Git-connected Vercel; GitHub Actions production HTTP smoke checks passed on 2026-10-14. The API is **PUBLIC** and contains only curated Markdown already published in this public repository. ## Routes ```http GET https://knowledgeai-nu.vercel.app/api/health GET https://knowledgeai-nu.vercel.app/api/search?q=TAKATAK&section=project&limit=5&offset=0 ``` `GET /api/health` reports `status`, `component`, `catalog_version` and `records`. HTTP 200 means the deployed function loaded its public corpus; 503 means catalog data is missing/invalid. `GET /api/search` accepts: | Parameter | Meaning | Constraints | | --- | --- | --- | | `q` | Search terms (all must match) | optional; max 120 characters and 12 words; accent-insensitive | | `section` | Source category | `all` (default), `guide`, `standard`, `project`, `prompt` | | `limit` | Results per page | integer 1–50; default 20 | | `offset` | Pagination offset | integer 0–999999; default 0 | HTTP 200 response contains `version: 1`, `visibility: "public"`, `source`, `query`, `section`, `total`, `limit`, `offset` and `results`. Each result includes `title`, `summary`, `section`, `path`, `source_id`, `source_sha256`, `source_url` and a bounded `excerpt`. `source_sha256` is SHA-256 over the original public Markdown file's **UTF-8 bytes**, used to detect content changes; it does not prove signing, access permissions or confidentiality. Bad query parameters yield HTTP 400. Write methods yield HTTP 405; this API does not accept or store uploads or private text. No cross-origin credential sharing is enabled. ## Examples ```sh curl -fsS 'https://knowledgeai-nu.vercel.app/api/search?q=ON2GO&section=project&limit=3' curl -fsS 'https://knowledgeai-nu.vercel.app/api/health' ``` Search results are only evidence pointers to *public curated documents*. Before executing consequential changes, an agent must read original GitHub source and current product repository state. ## Confidential material — forbidden here Do not send private source documents, customer data, authorization tokens or API keys to these public URLs. TAKATAK Auth, tenant/product entitlements, durable private storage, per-agent permissions and audit must be implemented and tested in a separate authenticated service before any private ingestion is enabled. See [ingestion policy](./03-INGESTION-POLICY.md) and [task queue](./TASK_QUEUE.md). ## CI Run `node --test tests/public-api.test.cjs` and `python3 -m unittest discover -s ingest/tests -v`; on `main`, `Knowledge Catalog CI` refreshes the catalog and checks live production HTTP endpoints. The production run must be **success** before claiming a verified release.

items.search_text: # TAKATAK ↔ private KnowledgeAI: issuer integration contract **Status: tested server-only cryptographic component, NOT wired into TAKATAK main, NOT deployed.** ## Reuse existing central authority TAKATAK master (repository `takatakca/takatak-v1`) already has `getServerAccessContext()` (`src/lib/security/access-context.ts`), `hasEffectivePermission()` (`src/lib/security/effective-permissions.ts`), and server-side membership resolution. Do NOT create another user directory or trust a client-provided `workspace_id`, product grant or role. The standalone pure Node component is `private-knowledge/integrations/takatak-issuer.cjs`. It returns an RS256 60-second `knowledgeai` JWT, and a separate public JWKS representation. The unit tests verify signatures against the existing `private-knowledge/src/auth.cjs` verifier and test key rotation. ## Required integration wiring inside TAKATAK 1. Read a REAL authenticated server session using `getServerAccessContext()`. Require `access.mode === 'client_scoped'`, an active authenticated membership, and the selected `activeClientId` belonging to `allowedClientIds`. Never issue from `foundation_demo`, `selection_required`, `platform_admin`, or any denied/inactive account. 2. Query TAKATAK's authoritative service/product entitlement for the selected client. **No KnowledgeAI-specific entitlement is currently confirmed**; fail closed until a product provisioning rule is explicitly defined and operational. Do not infer this from an unrelated `ai_studio` or `custom` service, or from a platform administrator role. 3. Map each requested scope (`knowledge:read`, `knowledge:write`, `knowledge:delete`, `knowledge:export`) to an explicitly APPROVED server-side permission/role policy, using `hasEffectivePermission()` where applicable. Do not treat generic `view_dashboard` as a KnowledgeAI grant and never accept an arbitrary requested scope from a browser without authorization. 4. From this same server-side request context, call `issueKnowledgeToken()` with `resolveAccess`, `authorizeProduct`, `authorizeScope`. The three callbacks MUST use trusted server-resolved data/database checks. Each issuance re-evaluates authorization; no cross-request user-level cache. 5. Provision a dedicated RSA 2048+ PEM signing key in a protected TAKATAK secret manager, with an explicit key ID (`kid`), HTTPS issuer origin, and a KnowledgeAI-only audience. Never commit secrets or write tokens to logs, HTML, localStorage, query strings or analytics. 6. Expose only `getKnowledgeJwks()` PUBLIC output at a dedicated, verified HTTPS JWKS endpoint; use a KnowledgeAI-only `kid` and keys, NOT TAKATAK's existing Bluesky OAuth JWKS. Rotate keys with overlapping public-key support at the issuer endpoint during token expiry windows. 7. Keep token exchange server-to-server through a protected gateway; the private KnowledgeAI service validates issuer, audience, signature, single operation scope and token lifetime, then independently checks its own workspace entitlement, revocations, RLS, quotas and source approvals. ## Secret/config contract — names only - TAKATAK server: dedicated signing private key PEM (never browser-exposed), approved HTTPS issuer origin, audience and active key ID. - KnowledgeAI private backend: `KNOWLEDGE_JWT_ISSUER`, `KNOWLEDGE_JWT_AUDIENCE`, `KNOWLEDGE_JWKS_URL`, `PRIVATE_DATABASE_URL`. - Dedicated private PostgreSQL: migration owner and separate non-owner runtime login, verified TLS trust, encrypted offsite backups, approval-control operator and reconciled tenant entitlements. ## Verified test coverage and limitations Run `node --test private-knowledge/tests/takatak-issuer.test.cjs`. CI checks signature compatibility, exact claims, 60-second expiry, fresh per-call authorization, denied workspaces, product/permission denials, non-RSA/weak keys, tampering, public JWKS field secrecy and rotation. Tests use an ephemeral locally generated RSA key and synthetic workspaces. They do NOT demonstrate that a real TAKATAK user has KnowledgeAI access, that TAKATAK has a configured signing key or endpoint, or that confidential KnowledgeAI databases are running. **Next:** define/provision the dedicated product entitlement in the TAKATAK master authority, implement and validate its authenticated issuer/JWKS routes there without changing the TAKATAK homepage, install the approved signing key outside GitHub, verify two real staging memberships, and only then connect to a separately provisioned confidential KnowledgeAI backend. ## 2026-10-16 — first proposed TAKATAK implementation The draft master [PR #195](https://github.com/takatakca/takatak-v1/pull/195) now implements a master-side `issuer.ts` and an explicit `KnowledgeAIWorkspaceGrant` model (separate from `ai_studio`). The proposed `POST /api/integrations/knowledgeai/search` route requires a real session, current per-scope grant, same-origin request and bounded payload; it signs a short-lived token **only on TAKATAK server** and proxies to an independent confidential KnowledgeAI endpoint. `GET /api/integrations/knowledgeai/jwks` returns only the public signing parameters when enabled. CI, migration review, secrets and actual staging tests are still pending. This is a proposal, not a deployed issuer. ## 2026-10-16 — merge coordination and live authentication safeguards [TAKATAK PR #195](https://github.com/takatakca/takatak-v1/pull/195) baseline CI [38884205088](https://github.com/takatakca/takatak-v1/actions/runs/38884205088) passed. Subsequent change `5f76e0bee202162c9569b01ef0f52372211ab98b` registers `/api/integrations/knowledgeai/search` as a high-risk path so the existing TAKATAK Supabase access resolver must obtain a fresh verified user instead of a cached local session. Regression coverage was added to `scripts/identity-isolation-tests.ts`. PR #194 defines a different grant model and exposes a different protected internal token route; select one authoritative grant/JWKS contract before merging PR #195. The private read-only proxy pattern remains preferred for browser calls because tokens stay server-side. Neither draft is deployed.

Further production gates: implement approved export/data portability; defined retention for audit/receipts/backups; authoritative token revocation and membership checks; private runtime observability, backup/restore and separate hosting. The source lifecycle code and migration 002 are tested but **not live**. Private version export: **code and synthetic CI integration DONE**, production BLOCKED. New `knowledge:export` scope, SQL-bound 10-version pagination, audit event, and tenant isolation. Requires migration 003 and a real approved trusted issuer before deployment. Remaining high-priority gaps: authoritative revocation, retention/deletion of backups and audit, secure private runtime and live end-to-end tests. Private inventory paging: DONE IN CODE/CI (limit 1–50, offset max 999999, verified cross-tenant pagination in `38630925562`). Operations remain BLOCKED IN PRODUCTION until actual TAKATAK identity/entitlement issuer and confidential PostgreSQL are verified. ### 2026-10-15 private authorization checklist - DONE IN CODE: deny-by-default workspace grants, JTI revocation, scoped SQL RLS, TLS/role/schema startup preflight, source-list HTTP offset regression and CI coverage. - BLOCKED IN PRODUCTION: TAKATAK authority must provide verified membership/product entitlements and a trusted RS256 token issuer/JWKS, and must govern writes to the admin access-control tables. - BLOCKED IN PRODUCTION: separate approved private PostgreSQL, TLS trust configuration, migration-owner + restricted runtime login, backups/recovery, access revocation operations, retention and live smoke tests. - DO NOT interpret synthetic CI identities, hard-coded test fixture entitlements or a Vercel READY status as evidence of active confidential production ingestion. TLS downgrade prevention: DONE IN CODE. PostgreSQL URLs with overriding SSL options are rejected and unit-tested. An approved real certificate chain and dedicated private deployment remain blocked externally. ### 2026-10-15 — backup restore readiness - DONE IN CI: `pg_dump -Fc` and `pg_restore` to a fresh database, with post-restore cross-workspace RLS, audit, revocation and deletion assertions (run 38801324564). - BLOCKED IN PRODUCTION: approved encrypted offsite backups, WAL/PITR, separate backup authority, key custody, retention/deletion policy, tested RPO/RTO and a staging restore drill using true TAKATAK entitlements. ### 2026-10-15 — tenant-scoped request quotas - DONE IN CODE/CI: atomic DB quota windows per tenant and permission, tested 429 denial, tenant-separated counters, FORCE RLS and restored quota state. - PENDING PRODUCTION: apply migration 005 as approved migration owner, grant restricted SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE on request_windows, configure independent gateway abuse protection and monitor agreed limits. - PENDING GOVERNANCE: approved expired-bucket retention and maintenance schedule (NO automatic deletion job exists). Do not use quotas as billing. ### 2026-10-15 — retention maintenance - DONE IN CODE/CI: preview-first, privileged maintenance for aged quota buckets, replay receipts and expired token revocations with explicit two-flag opt-in, bounded batches, advisory locking and synthetic PostgreSQL regression tests. - BLOCKED IN PRODUCTION: agreed retention periods, legal holds, authorized operator/service account, protected run logs, encrypted backups and separately approved scheduling. **Audit/document erasure is NOT implemented.** ### 2026-10-15 — private source approval gate - DONE IN CODE: explicit per-workspace source approval and exact HTTPS URL validation before write, expiry checks, admin-only approval management, FORCE RLS and private synthetic integration tests (migration 006). - STILL BLOCKED: approved TAKATAK administrative source-review/ownership and privacy classification workflow, real issuer, dedicated private DB and production ingestion/staging verification.
